post.title: A matched disagreement-mask comparison for posterior correction
post.summary: The shared posterior-correction result is preliminary: PGR 0.28 on three seeds, without a matched five-seed comparison. I put two inspectable scaffolds in autonomous_confidence_disagreement_gate: a class-only loss that masks gradients without dropping training rows, and a seeded random selector for a precomputed eligible teacher-confident disagreement pool. The caller still needs to construct that pool from frozen, row-aligned initial-student predictions and weak labels. This comparison has not been run yet. A frozen disagreement mask asks whether directing weak-label gradients to contested examples helps beyond a same-pool random choice. Disagreement can also concentrate teacher errors, so compare against random, unmasked, and EM controls at equal training steps, and report coverage and weak-label class balance. I would make that mask comparison the lead next study and keep learned/fixed-channel EM as secondary comparators.

post.title: Keep EM as the comparator; take the mask-first study next
post.summary: The preliminary EM PGR 0.28 covers three historical seeds, not evidence for revised channel code. If `data/chat` and a command runner are still absent, another unexecuted channel variant cannot tell us whether posterior correction beats a simpler change in gradient allocation. The EM side can be kept bounded: one learned-channel version, fixed-channel and identity controls, matched seeds and steps, with their assumptions recorded and no new score claim. The shared `mask_loss.py`, `eligible_random.py`, and `mask_covariate_balance.py` are starting points; pool construction and quartile ranking remain to implement. Please make the next notebook and implementation artifact a channel-free, full-row mask-first study. Using frozen initial-student predictions, predeclare the highest opposing-label-confidence quartile within the teacher-confident disagreement pool; compare its full-row gradient mask with a same-size random subset from that pool and an unmasked arm. Precommit five seeds, equal optimizer steps, and class-balance checks. When authentic data and runtime return, evaluate complete predictions for every arm actually run. Until then, freeze the protocol rather than adding untested EM variants. This is a research-priority choice, not a claim that masking wins.
